chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: Bands heard on radio, and Speed Webb's Hollywood Blue Devils
summary: He heard the big bands on national radio hookups; Speed Webb's band later held Vic Dickenson, the Eldridges and the Wilsons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And you heard Chick Webb in Chicago?
No, I heard him on broadcasts, from New York out here. Like, I heard any number of bands on broadcast. They'd had national hookup out here, you know. On Saturdays, or something like that.
Who else did you hear that made an impression?

Oh, I heard the Rhythm Band. I heard the Blue Rhythm Band. I thought it was at first Mills Blue Rhythm Band. But it was just the Rhythm Band. I heard Don Redman. I heard Claude Hopkins, Fletcher Henderson. Who else, who else, who else? I heard the Mills Brothers. Of course, I'd heard them first on the Lucky Strike Show, in the early 30's, when they were first discovered.

Oh, I heard any number of bands. Like, every week they had different bands, you know, that I heard in California, in Los Angeles. And then one week, Louis Armstrong's band played the whole week, broadcast. I heard Duke, naturally. And they had a poll going on then that I was unaware of, until I was almost out of high school. And like, a poll ran something like Duke Ellington, Fletcher Henderson, Don Redman.

Oh, this other band that I was trying to think of -- Speed Webb. He was around the Midwest. Speed Webb and his Blue Devils. He -- Speed Webb was a leader, singer, and he also played drums. And he had a band called Speed Webb's Hollywood Blue Devils.

No. He was from around Buffalo, Indianapolis. He just barnstormed, you know. But he wound up out here and he named his band that. And guess who he had in the band? He had Vic Dickenson, he had Roy and Joe Eldridge, Gus Wilson

and Teddy Wilson. And Eli Robinson and Reunald Jones, who we called Jonesy. So that was quite a band. Two brothers, sets, you know. The Wilson brothers and the Eldridge brothers. That was something else.
